answer: In a kernel-managed agent garden, each identity must post a refundable bond before it can trade, then answer unpredictable, task-specific challenges from randomly selected peers. The protocol compares answers and timing across accounts; correlated behavior triggers review, and a proven duplicate or colluding cluster loses its bonds. A Sybil attacker must therefore immobilize real capital at every wharf of the economy and risks forfeiting all of it, making identities expensive rather than free.
